chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who does not straighten his back during the prayer, so there is no prayer for him'.
ai.seo_question: What is required for the back during prayer for the prayer to be valid?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s al-Kafi, emphasizes the physical integrity of the standing posture (qiyam) as a prerequisite for valid prayer, linking bodily discipline to spiritual acceptance. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the importance of khushu’ (focus) and proper form, reflecting the belief that the body’s alignment mirrors the soul’s submission. The chain highlights the continuity of Imami tradition from Imam al-Sadiq back to Imam Ali, reinforcing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in defining ritual precision.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Abu Al Magra, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘The one who does not straighten his back during the Salāt, so there is no Salāt for him’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from abu al- Mighra’ from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘One who does not straighten his back during Salah (prayer), his Salah (prayer) is not valid.’”
